title: Regional egress fuse and soft-deny repair
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Fixes a scenario where regional egress fuse could flip to hard-deny under transient KV cache pressure; this soft-deny repair reduces customer request drop rate during regional perturbations.
description:
Context and motivation:
We observed a production incident (SUP-1021) where a sudden KV cache pressure and transient affinity loss in a single region caused the local egress fuse to transition into a hard-deny state too aggressively. That hard-deny prevented low-priority and retriable traffic from reaching fallback paths (regional reroute and cold-queue), causing elevated user-facing errors and SLO violations for synchronous generation requests.

Goal:
Introduce a repair to the regional egress fuse and the soft-deny path so that: 1) transient state flips do not immediately cause hard-deny; 2) soft-deny policy admits low-cost retriable requests and routes heavier requests to compatible variants; 3) telemetry surfaces fuse state transitions and rejection classes more clearly for on-call.

Summary of changes (high level):
- Add exponential cooloff + minimum observation window to egress_fuse state transitions to avoid flip-flopping under short-lived KV pressure spikes.
- Introduce a soft-deny admission filter that marks requests as "deferable" and allows them to be enqueued for regional cold-queue or routed to a lower-cost replica if available.
- Make receiver-side metrics emit rejection class tags: hard_deny, soft_deny_deferred, soft_deny_reroute.
- Add guard in SLO enforcer to avoid double-accounting of deferred requests when computing immediate violation risk.
- Small config knobs surfaced via helm configmap: egressFuse.minWindowMs, egressFuse.cooldownFactor, softDeny.admitPolicy.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for state machine transitions (egress_fuse_test.go)
- [x] Integration test that simulates transient cache pressure and asserts no hard-deny within 500ms window
- [x] Observability updates (alerts + dashboard snippet)
- [x] Rollback plan documented
- [x] Security review (no new data plane auth changes)

Commits (summary):
- add: cooldown and window logic to runtime/egress_fuse.go
- add: admission filter and routing hook for soft-deny in pkg/egress/soft_deny.go
- fix: SLO enforcer double-count protection in pkg/slo/enforcer.go
- docs: operational runbook and helm config defaults in docs/operational/egress-fuse.md
- test: integration to simulate kv pressure in tests/integration/egress_fuse_test.go

Files changed (high level):
src/runtime/egress_fuse.go (core state machine + tests)
pkg/egress/soft_deny.go (new)
pkg/slo/enforcer.go (accounting fix)
deploy/helm/redwood/templates/configmap.yaml (expose knobs)
observability/alerts.yaml (new alert rule)
docs/operational/egress-fuse.md (runbook)
tests/integration/egress_fuse_test.go (integration scenario)

Testing and CI notes:
- Initial CI run failed intermittently in the integration job (egress-fuse-integration) due to a flaky test harness timeout; reran that job with a longer timeout and it passed. All unit tests green and linting clean.
- Local staging validation run with a synthetic load reproducer (kv-pressure-sim) shows failure rate drop from ~6.2% to ~0.9% for low-priority requests during a 30s spike; no measurable latency regression for p50/p90 of high-priority paths.

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy to canary region behind feature flag softDeny.enabled=false and monitor metrics for 10 minutes.
2) Enable softDeny.enabled=true in canary and run synthetic injection for 5m.
3) Gradual roll to remaining regions over three 15-minute windows, monitor rejection_class metrics and SLO delta.

Backout plan:
- Revert helm values to previous configmap (egressFuse.* and softDeny.*) and promote previous image; config rollback is safe and does not require DB changes.

Operational notes:
- New metrics: redwood.egress_fuse.state (enum), redwood.egress_reject.class (labels), redwood.soft_deny.enqueue_count. Alerts: soft-deny-rate > 2% sustained for 5m triggers SRE paging.

Why this is different from previous effort:
Most prior PRs implemented broad tenant quarantine or eviction approaches. This change focuses narrowly on the egress decision surface: minimize hard-deny cases by introducing temporal smoothing and a defensive soft-deny path that preserves request durability (deferred queuing or reroute) instead of immediate drop. The intent is graceful degradation with measurable SLO impact reduction.

Observed limitations / open follow-ups:
- softDeny.admitPolicy default admits only low-cost retriable requests; follow-up will broaden policy to include small-batch embeddings after further load testing (ENG-1950).
- Need to add trace-span tagging for soft-deny decisions in a separate perf PR to avoid adding runtime overhead here.

Related work: ENG-1892 (design doc), SUP-1021 (incident), SRE-44 (postmortem action).
